transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Jordan Meyer (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (CTO, Mosaic Labs), Leah Torres (ML Eng), Samir Khan (Infra), Rina Patel (Product)

Auto-Summary: quick econ audit, focused on tokens/sec/$ and caching wins; some noisy transcription. Action items captured.

Topics: tokens/sec per dollar, prefix/KV cache savings, batching thresholds and latency impact, dedicated vs hosted routing, quantization tradeoffs.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Jordan Meyer: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, um quick roll call — Jordan here from Redwood, Priya's with me, you'll - you all good on audio? 
[00:08] Ethan Park: yeah good, Ethan here, can hear you. sorry running late, just grabbed a coffee.
[00:12] Priya Desai: hi Ethan, Leah, Samir, nice to meet you, I'll be driving the bench numbers later in the call.
[00:18] Leah Torres: hi all, Leah — wanted to highlight upfront that our production prompt lengths are a little all over, mean about 520 tokens, tail to 3k for a small percent.
[00:27] Samir Khan: we also have a spiky pattern around 11am PST where traffic doubles for ~20 minutes.
[00:33] Jordan: perfect, that's exactly the profile we need. goal today — review last week's pilot metrics, double-check tokens/sec per dollar, and agree on tuning steps.
[00:42] Ethan: sounds good, particularly interested in caching numbers you mentioned in the Slack note, you said 20-30% savings?
[00:49] Priya: yeah, I did quick sim against your sample dataset — with prefix/KV cache enabled we saw around 27% cost reduction in token counts used for identical prefixes; that's simulated with 95% confidence interval ±3% but real-world can vary based on prompt uniqueness.
[01:02] Leah: ok, can you explain the sim? like, did you account for the tail cases with long context? our long-tail prompts could reduce cache hit ratio.
[01:10] Priya: good call. sim used the 10k request sample you shared — we split by prompt fingerprint and computed prefix reuse at various ngram cutoffs; the 27% assumes a conservative 512-token prefix match; with 1k prefix match we saw up to 35% savings but that relies on more repeated context.
[01:26] Samir: interesting. what about KV cache memory pressure? our infra team is concerned about GPU memory overhead with large KV caches and many concurrent sessions.
[01:34] Priya: yes, we modelled memory. tradeoff: larger KV cache increases hit rate but can raise per-worker memory 5-12% depending on sequence length. Redwood runtime supports sharded KV cache and TTL eviction — for your traffic we suggested a per-session cap of 256k entries, which kept overhead to ~6% and preserved most hits.
[01:52] Ethan: ok that seems reasonable. let's talk about tokens/sec per dollar. last week your dashboard showed 1400 tokens/sec per dollar for the quantized variant — that number confused my finance team.
02:02 Speaker 1: mm-hmm
[02:05] Priya: right, so tokens/sec/$ is a derived metric — we take throughput (tokens/sec) at burst and divide by cost/sec for that instance profile. For the quantized 4-bit model on A100-equivalent we measured sustained 1100 tps, cost normalized to your committed price produced ~1400 tps per USD. the important part is this is workload dependent — fewer decoder steps or thicker batching changes it.
[02:31] Leah: and packing/batching — what's the sweet spot for latency? our SLO is 300ms p95 for the interactive path.
[02:38] Priya: if we set batching window 15ms and max batch size 16 we saw p95 ~320-350ms with throughput gains ~28%. dropping window to 5ms gave p95 ~260ms but throughput fall to ~15% gain. So it's a lat-vs-cost dial.
[02:56] Jordan: to paraphrase — short window gives lower latency at higher unit cost, longer window better tokens/sec per dollar but risks p95 swelling.
[03:04] Rina Patel: how would dedicated capacity change this math? is it worth the switch during POC?
[03:09] Priya: Dedicated gives predictable cost per-month and you can pin GPUs; it smooths unit cost especially at scale with high sustained queries. For your spiky 11am pattern, dedicated + autoscale with burst pools helps keep latency; for small pilot volumes hosted is fine but you pay more on peak.
[03:25] Ethan: we'd prefer to avoid heavy commitment yet — can we emulate dedicated performance in hosted via reserved bursts? or is there falloff?
[03:33] Jordan: there's a burst pool for hosted customers, you can cap on minute-level; it's not identical but reasonably close. Priya: any perf caveats?
[03:40] Priya: difference is cold-starts and scheduling jitter; dedicated reduces jitter but hosted burst is cheaper to trial.
[03:45] Samir: security question — if we enable cache, does anything persist outside our VPC? audit logs? KMS?
[03:51] Jordan: caching occurs within the runtime and for Private/VPC deployments stays customer-only. For hosted we encrypt with KMS and we can enable short-lived keys, SOC2 controls apply. I'll share the SOC2 pack after the call.
[04:04] Leah: thanks. can you also share a sample config for batching we can try in staging?
[04:08] Priya: yes — I'll send a 'batching playbook' with 3 configs: ultra-low-latency (5ms/4), balanced (10-15ms/8-16), throughput-first (30ms/32). I'll include recommended kv cache caps and TTLs.
[04:22] Ethan: let's talk numbers concretely — if we take your recommended balanced config, what's expected token/sec per dollar and p95?
[04:30] Priya: balanced on quantized model gave us ~1800 tokens/sec per dollar in sim and p95 about 320ms on your 520-token mean; without caching it's ~1400 tps/$ so caching adds ~28% improvement in that scenario.
[04:45] Rina: what's the impact of quantization to output quality? product cares about hallucination rates.
[04:50] Priya: we measured few-shot evals on your in-domain tests — 4-bit quant introduced a 1.5% delta in accuracy metrics for extraction tasks, higher for open-ended summarization (~3% delta). tradeoff: big cost savings vs slight quality delta; we can test mixed strategy: quantized for high-volume non-critical paths, full-fp for sensitive tasks.
[05:10] Ethan: accepted. curious about metrics for tokens/sec per dollar under mixed routing — e.g., route 70% to quantized and 30% to higher-precision; any back-of-envelope?
[05:18] Priya: ballpark: weighted tokens/sec/$ = 0.7*1800 + 0.3*900 = 1530 tps/$, so still better than full-fp alone. But you must account for differential latency and cost of A/B routing.
[05:33] Samir: regarding benchmarks — can Redwood run a targeted bench with our anonymized payloads to measure cache hit, memory overhead, and p95 under 2x spiky load?
[05:41] Jordan: yes, we'll schedule a bench. Priya will run it on Monday; we'll do two runs: caching on/off, batch balanced, n=3.
[05:48] Leah: also please include a test with 1k prefix threshold since we have many templates with long repeated preambles.
[05:53] Priya: will do, adding 512 and 1k prefix thresholds.
[05:56] Ethan: one more ops question — what telemetry will we see in your console to monitor tokens/sec/$ and cache hit rate?
06:02 Speaker 2: mm
[06:03] Jordan: Console exposes per-route token counters, per-model cost, cache_hit_rate, kv_evictions, and per-token latencies with traces; we can give dashboard templates.
[06:12] Rina: Great. Anything else on tradeoffs or blockers we should be aware of?
[06:17] Priya: just rollover: watch out for long-tail prompts reducing cache efficacy; ensure prompt normalization before fingerprinting to maximize hits. Also recommend prefix canonicalization — strip timestamps/IDs.
[06:30] Ethan: got it. last, timeline: if bench looks good, we may want to expand pilot to prod-like volume in two weeks. can you support a pilot scale run week of 6/1?
[06:39] Jordan: yes, we can scope a week-of-6/1 ramp test assuming data and configs by 5/25.
[06:44] Leah: ok I'll send the samples tonight and note which endpoints are interactive vs async.
[06:49] Jordan: perfect. quick recap and next steps — Priya to run benchmarks, Jordan to send SOC2 and network diagram, Mosaic to share payloads and traffic histogram. we'll reconvene next Thursday same time unless we need ad-hoc.
[06:59] Ethan: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:02] Jordan: thanks all, bye.

---- End Transcript ----

Questions captured: what are recommended batching windows for p95 300ms? (see playbook), how to canonicalize prefixes for best cache? (Priya will add examples).

Notes on transcription: occasional label speaker 1/2, minor mis-hears ("kv cache" as "k-v cash"), timestamps approximate.
